title.narrative: Design and delivery of employment and skills policy improved at central and local levels

description.narrative: Bosnia and Herzegovina faces persistent labour market challenges, including high youth unemployment, low labour force participation, and limited access to quality Technical Vocational Education and Ttraining (TVET). Active labour market policies are mostly focused on employment subsidies and not training programs and are insufficiently diversified. The fragmented governance structure complicates the adoption of common policies, affecting the responsiveness of TVET to labour market needs, the use of modern teaching methodologies, and the development of core skills like entrepreneurship. To address these gaps, the ILO supports TVET reform through the development of 17 occupational standards and nine qualification standards, alongside teacher training programmes in digital content creation and entrepreneurship. These efforts aim to improve the quality and relevance of TVET, ensuring young people acquire the skills needed for sustainable employment. In parallel, the ILO works to strengthen local employment partnerships (LEPs) as key tools for activation and labour market integration, supporting the establishment of six additional LEPs to tailor activation measures to local needs. Special attention is given to building the capacity of employment offices to design and implement effective active labour market measures (ALMPs), particularly for youth, rural women, and vulnerable groups. Furthermore, through the EU-ILO Technical Assistance Facility, the ILO supports Bosnia and Herzegovina in finalizing its Youth Guarantee Implementation Plan, aligning activation services with EU standards to ensure young people receive quality employment, training, or education opportunities. The ILO supports the design and testing of five new pathways for labour market transition of vulnerable individuals. By enhancing skills development and fostering inclusive employment strategies, these efforts contribute to stronger labour market outcomes and economic resilience.
